item: One clause on the lane-heuristic bullet saying that what earlier reviews cost is evidence for the lane choice and never a ceiling to come under, plus the reason: a review that needed its cost was worth it.
outflow: Nothing had a cheaper home. The clause has to sit where the lane is chosen, and the only material a lane choice loads is this body -- a reference is opened after the lane is picked, and the records cell that defines the cost field is loaded at the close. The draft was cut from 165 characters to 138, which is the added run including its joining space; both of its halves survived that cut, the 27 characters that went being wording spread across them. Nothing in the body sheds further without restructuring the cell, which is a change this one does not carry.

item: The two rules the affirmed brief agreed, both of which have to be readable before any reference is opened. (1) The one-round shape, stated where the pipeline's stages are enumerated, because a session choosing the lane loads only this body. (2) The record-honesty rider in the evidence standards: the change's own record and the review's own record held to honesty whatever a claim's load, and neither reaching the pre-implementation artifact or the brief it carries. Net of the pointer text the same change deletes. Sized against the tree this change's review-fix batch produced, not the pre-review tree.
outflow: Applied, and it turned up two genuine shed candidates and no move. Neither rule relocates: the record-honesty rider binds what a seat files, and arbitration.md -- the only reference that could host a disposition rule -- states outright that a prosecution seat does not need it, so a rule seats must obey cannot live where seats never read; the one-round shape must be readable when the lane is chosen, which is before any reference opens. The two candidates are existing sections, not the addition: `Choosing the shape`, which only the dispatching session needs, and `Closing a recurring class`, which only a stage promoting or retiring a lens needs. Both pass the disqualifier and either would fit this addition, but each is a restructuring of the cell rather than a move -- shedding the second would split a lens retirement across arbitration.md, which rules it, and the-record.md, which reports it -- and this change's affirmed boundary does not carry a restructuring. #357's row said nothing sheds without restructuring; that was re-checked here rather than inherited, and it is the restructuring, not the absence of candidates, that is the reason. Filed as its own item.

item: The 121 characters admitted for the lane-heuristic clause come back: the body is under its 9,000 ceiling again without that admission, so the room is banked rather than left standing for whatever is added next.
outflow: This change gave the both-polarities rule one owner. The duplicated statement, its negative-control requirement and the #142 incident that is that requirement's reason left this cell for skills/substrate/SKILL.md, the cell a session fires when it is writing the guard rather than reviewing one. Nothing was trimmed to make this room and nothing was deleted -- the text moved, and the ceiling is answered by the move.
